decomposition_notes: Multi-goal split along the three orthogonal seams from the Sketch section. G1 (events + queue) emits notification_requested into Oban; G2 (preferences UI) lets users opt in to channels and configure DND; G3 (email rendering + dispatch) consumes the queue and emails out. G1 and G2 are independent and can be claimed in any order. G3 depends on G1 — claim G1 first, let its queue contract land in main, then claim G3. G2 is fully parallel.

goals.title: Wire notification event detection and Oban queue
goals.why: Approval lag p50 is 28h because time-sensitive events only surface in-app; events must reach an out-of-band channel via a deduping queue.
goals.what: Emit notification_requested from approval lifecycle / comment mentions / dependency-unblocked, and land them on an Oban queue keyed by recipient + event class so a recipient never gets the same event twice.
goals.description: Independent of UI and email work; produces the queue contract both downstream goals depend on.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Approval lifecycle emits notification_requested when an approval is owed
Comment mentions emit notification_requested at create time
Dependency-unblocked emits notification_requested
Oban queue dedupes by (recipient_id, event_class)
pitfalls: Do not introduce a new background-job library; reuse the existing Oban setup

tasks.title: Define notification_requested event shape and module
tasks.description: Add MyApp.Notifications.Event struct with recipient_id, event_class, payload, occurred_at. Used as the queue input contract.
tasks.why: Every emitter and the queue need one agreed contract; without a typed event shape the three emit sites will drift.
tasks.what: Define MyApp.Notifications.Event struct (recipient_id, event_class, payload, occurred_at) with a constructor that enforces required fields.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Event struct defined
Unit test asserts struct construction + required fields
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use @enforce_keys plus a new/1 constructor returning {:ok, event} | {:error, reason}
Keep event_class a closed set (:approval_owed, :mention, :dependency_unblocked)
pitfalls: Do not let payload become a dumping ground — keep it to what the templates need
Do not couple the struct to Oban job args yet; the queue task owns that mapping

unit_tests: new/1 with all fields returns the struct
Missing recipient_id or event_class returns an error
Unknown event_class is rejected
integration_tests: Not applicable — pure struct module with no collaborators yet
manual_tests: Not applicable — covered by unit tests
edge_cases: occurred_at defaults sensibly when omitted
payload accepts an empty map

security_considerations: Payload will carry PII (names, comment excerpts) downstream — keep fields minimal and never log full payloads at info level

tasks.title: Add :notifications Oban queue config
tasks.description: Register the new :notifications queue in the existing Oban config with a sensible concurrency limit.
tasks.why: The dispatcher and dedupe logic need a dedicated supervised queue; sharing the default queue would let unrelated jobs starve notifications.
tasks.what: Register a :notifications queue in the existing Oban config with a concurrency limit sized to the SMTP relay's rate cap.
tasks.where_context: config/config.exs (Oban queues key), config/test.exs (inline/manual testing mode)
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Queue is supervised
Concurrency limit set to a value that respects SMTP relay limits
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mirror the existing Oban queue entries in config.exs
Use Oban's testing mode in the test env like the other queues
pitfalls: Do not set concurrency higher than the SMTP relay allows — bounced jobs retry and amplify load
Do not forget test-env config; async tests hang on live queues

unit_tests: Config test asserts the Oban queues include :notifications with the expected limit
integration_tests: mix compile succeeds and the app boots in dev with the queue supervised
edge_cases: Test environment runs jobs inline/manually so nothing executes in the background
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Config assertion only — no logic to cover

security_considerations: None directly — configuration only; the concurrency cap is the throttle protecting the mail relay from accidental floods

tasks.title: Emit notification_requested from approval lifecycle
tasks.description: Hook the existing approval-state-transition path so an 'approval owed to X' transition emits a notification_requested event to the queue.
tasks.why: Approval-owed is the highest-value event class — the 28h p50 approval lag is the metric this initiative exists to move.
tasks.what: Hook the approval state-transition path so an 'approval owed to X' transition builds a Notifications.Event and enqueues it.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Approval owed transition emits event
Unit test asserts an event is enqueued when the approval is created
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Emit inside the same Ecto.Multi as the state transition so event and state change commit atomically
Build the event via Event.new/1, never a bare map
pitfalls: Do not emit on every transition — only the transition that creates an owed approval
Decide and test the failure mode when enqueue fails; it must not silently roll back the approval

unit_tests: Creating an owed approval enqueues exactly one :approval_owed event for the approver
Non-owed transitions enqueue nothing
integration_tests: Full approval create flows through to an Oban job, asserted via Oban.Testing
manual_tests: Not applicable — covered by Oban.Testing assertions
edge_cases: Approver is the approval author (self) — decide suppress vs send and test it
Approval reassigned before dispatch leaves a stale recipient
testing_strategy.coverage_target: All lifecycle transition branches that can emit

security_considerations: Recipient is derived server-side from the approval record — never from request params
Payload carries IDs and titles only, not full approval bodies, to limit PII sitting in the jobs table

tasks.title: Emit notification_requested from comment mentions
tasks.description: On comment create, scan for @mentions and emit one notification_requested event per mentioned user.
tasks.why: Mentions are a direct ask for someone's attention; they are the second event class the spec commits to.
tasks.what: On comment create, scan the body for @mentions, resolve them to users, and emit one notification_requested per unique mentioned user.
tasks.where_context: lib/app/comments/mentions.ex (new scanner + emitter), comment create path in lib/app/comments/
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Mention scanning emits one event per unique user
Unit test covers single mention, multi-mention, self-mention (suppressed)
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Resolve mentions with exact-match username lookups, not LIKE scans
Emit after the comment insert commits, inside the same Multi
pitfalls: Self-mentions are suppressed per the acceptance criteria
Duplicate @alice @alice in one comment must produce one event, not two

unit_tests: Single mention emits one event
Multiple distinct mentions emit one event each
Self-mention emits nothing
Repeated mention of the same user collapses to one event
integration_tests: Comment create path enqueues the expected Oban jobs
manual_tests: Not applicable — covered by unit and integration tests
edge_cases: @nonexistent-user resolves to nothing and emits nothing
Mention-like text inside code fences or email addresses (a@b.com) must not false-positive
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Scanner covered across all mention shapes

security_considerations: Comment text is untrusted input — keep the scanner regex safe against pathological input (ReDoS); the excerpt in the payload is raw text escaped later at render time
Only notify users authorized to see the commented task — a mention must not leak private task activity

tasks.title: Emit notification_requested when a dependency is unblocked
tasks.description: When a task's last blocking dependency completes, emit notification_requested for the task's owner.
tasks.why: Owners of blocked tasks currently discover unblocks by polling the board; this event closes that gap.
tasks.what: When a task's last blocking dependency completes, emit notification_requested for the task's owner.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Dependency-unblock transition emits event
Unit test covers single-dep and chain-of-deps cases
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Compute 'last blocker' inside the completion transaction to avoid a race between concurrent completions
Reuse Event.new/1 and the shared enqueue entry point
pitfalls: Two blockers completing concurrently must not double-emit — the check and emit must be atomic
Unowned tasks have no recipient; skip the emit, do not crash

unit_tests: Completing the last blocker emits for the owner
Completing a non-last blocker emits nothing
Unowned task emits nothing
integration_tests: Chain-of-deps scenario: completing the upstream task emits only for the directly unblocked task's owner
edge_cases: Concurrent completion of the two final blockers yields exactly one event
Dependency removed (not completed) also unblocks — decide whether that emits and test it

security_considerations: Recipient derived from task ownership server-side; payload limited to task IDs/titles the owner already has access to

tasks.title: Implement queue dedupe by (recipient_id, event_class)
tasks.description: Before persisting an enqueued event, look up existing pending events for the same recipient + event class and collapse the payload into the existing job.
tasks.why: Bursty activity (five comments in one review) must not fan out into five emails; dedupe is the queue's core promise.
tasks.what: Before persisting an enqueued event, find pending jobs for the same (recipient_id, event_class) and merge the new payload into the existing job.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Duplicate events within a window collapse
Unit test asserts two enqueues of the same recipient+class produce one job
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Prefer Oban unique jobs over hand-rolled select-then-update
Merge payloads as an append-only list so no event data is lost in the collapse
pitfalls: Dedupe window trades against delivery latency — do not hold events until they go stale
A job already executing must not be mutated; only pending jobs merge

unit_tests: Two enqueues of the same recipient+class yield one job with a merged payload
Different recipients never merge
Different event classes never merge
integration_tests: Concurrent enqueues from two processes still yield one job — uniqueness enforced at the DB
edge_cases: Event enqueued while the worker holds the matching job
Merged payload preserves occurred_at ordering
testing_strategy.coverage_target: All dedupe/merge branches plus one concurrency test

security_considerations: The dedupe key must include recipient_id — a cross-recipient merge bug would deliver one user's events (PII) to another
Cap the merge count so an attacker spamming mentions cannot bloat a job row unboundedly

goals.title: Build user notification preferences UI
goals.why: Users must explicitly opt in to channels (CAN-SPAM + GDPR); without preferences, nothing can be sent.
goals.what: Add a preferences LiveView, the user_notification_preferences schema, per-event-class opt-in toggles, per-user DND window, and email-address override.
goals.description: Independent of G1 and G3. Can be claimed in parallel with either.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Preferences LiveView lets users opt in per event class
DND window persisted per user
Email-address override defaults to account email
Unsubscribe link in every notification routes back to this UI
pitfalls: Do not send any email to a user who has not explicitly opted in

tasks.title: Add user_notification_preferences schema and migration
tasks.description: Schema fields: user_id, channel (string), event_class (string), enabled (bool), dnd_start, dnd_end, email_override.
tasks.why: CAN-SPAM and GDPR require explicit opt-in; the schema is where 'nothing is sent by default' is enforced structurally.
tasks.what: Add the user_notification_preferences table and schema: user_id, channel, event_class, enabled (default false), dnd_start, dnd_end, email_override.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Schema + migration land
Default dnd window is 22:00-08:00 in the user's TZ
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mirror the existing migration style; unique index on (user_id, channel, event_class)
Use :time columns for dnd_start/dnd_end; TZ handling lives in the context, not the schema
pitfalls: enabled must default false at the DB level, not just the changeset — opt-in is a legal requirement
The default 22:00-08:00 DND window crosses midnight; store raw times and leave window math to dnd_active?

unit_tests: Changeset validates channel and event_class against the known sets
email_override rejects malformed addresses
enabled defaults to false
integration_tests: mix ecto.migrate and rollback both run cleanly; the unique index rejects duplicate (user, channel, event_class) rows
manual_tests: Not applicable — covered by changeset and migration tests
edge_cases: Row without DND values falls back to the 22:00-08:00 default
Nil email_override means the account email is used

security_considerations: enabled=false as the DB default is the opt-in guarantee — fail closed
Validate email_override strictly; it becomes an SMTP recipient downstream (header-injection surface)
Preferences are per-user PII; FK plus unique index keep rows tied to their owner

tasks.title: Add MyApp.Accounts.NotificationPreferences context
tasks.description: Context functions: get_preferences/1, update_preferences/2, channel_enabled?/3, dnd_active?/2. The dispatcher (G3) calls into this to decide whether to send.
tasks.why: The G3 dispatcher must not query preference rows directly; this context is the single decision seam for 'may I send?'.
tasks.what: Add the NotificationPreferences context: get_preferences/1, update_preferences/2, channel_enabled?/3, dnd_active?/2.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
All four functions exist and have tests
channel_enabled? defaults to false for unrecognized channels
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Follow the existing Accounts context style (take a user or user_id, return tagged tuples)
channel_enabled?/3 and dnd_active?/2 must be pure lookups safe to call from the Oban worker
pitfalls: channel_enabled? must default false for unknown channels AND for users with no preference row — fail closed both ways
dnd_active? must handle windows that cross midnight (22:00-08:00)

unit_tests: channel_enabled? is false for unknown channel, missing row, and enabled=false; true only when explicitly enabled
dnd_active? is true at 23:00 and 07:00 for a 22:00-08:00 window and false at 12:00
update_preferences rejects writes to another user's rows
integration_tests: Context round-trips against the real schema via DataCase
manual_tests: Not applicable — covered by unit and integration tests
edge_cases: Degenerate window where dnd_start equals dnd_end
User timezone change mid-window
testing_strategy.coverage_target: All decision branches — this gate protects legal compliance

security_considerations: Fail-closed defaults everywhere: no row, unknown channel, and nil enabled all mean do-not-send
update_preferences/2 receives request-derived params from the LiveView — writes must be scoped to the given user's rows only

tasks.title: Scaffold preferences LiveView mount and basic form
tasks.description: Mount loads the user's preferences via the context; render shows a per-event-class table with opt-in checkboxes.
tasks.why: Users need a place to opt in; until this page exists every channel stays legally off for everyone.
tasks.what: Preferences LiveView at /settings/notifications: mount loads the current user's prefs via the context, the form renders one opt-in row per event class, save persists atomically.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Route /settings/notifications maps to the LiveView
Form renders one row per event class
Saving updates the database atomically
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mount behind the existing require_authenticated_user on_mount hook
All reads and writes go through NotificationPreferences — never Repo in the LiveView
Use core_components form idioms
pitfalls: Save must be atomic across rows — a partial save leaves a user half-opted-in
Do not trust event_class values from form params; map them against the known set

unit_tests: Not applicable — decision logic lives in the context; view behavior covered by LiveView tests
integration_tests: LiveView test: mount renders one row per event class; toggling and saving persists via the context
manual_tests: Click through opt-in and save in the browser; reload confirms persistence
edge_cases: User with zero preference rows sees all toggles off
Form submit containing an unknown event_class is rejected
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Mount, save, and validation paths covered by LiveView tests

security_considerations: Route must sit in the authenticated scope — preferences are per-user PII
Persist only for socket.assigns.current_user; ignore any user identifier arriving in params
Allowlist channel/event_class params before they reach the changeset

tasks.title: Add DND time-window controls to preferences form
tasks.description: Add two time-picker inputs (start, end) for the user's DND window; persist on save.
tasks.why: Out-of-band notifications at 3am erode trust and get the channel muted; DND is the retention guard that makes opt-in durable.
tasks.what: Add start/end time-picker inputs to the preferences form, persisted to dnd_start/dnd_end, supporting windows that cross midnight.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Two time inputs render
Crossing midnight is supported (e.g., 22:00-08:00)
DND window persists across reloads
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use native time inputs via the core_components input idioms
Parse with Time.from_iso8601/1; store raw times — window math stays in dnd_active?/2
pitfalls: 22:00-08:00 crosses midnight — the UI must not helpfully swap start and end
Do not do window math in the view; the context owns it

verification_steps.step_text: Set DND window 22:00-08:00 and confirm dnd_active? returns true at 23:00

unit_tests: Changeset accepts valid times and rejects garbage strings
integration_tests: LiveView test: set 22:00-08:00, save, reload — values persist
dnd_active? returns true at 23:00 with the saved window
manual_tests: Set the window in a browser and verify the pickers round-trip the values
edge_cases: Equal start and end times
Clearing the window reverts to the 22:00-08:00 default
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Time parsing and persistence branches covered

security_considerations: Time inputs are user input — parse strictly with Time.from_iso8601, never interpolate into queries
No new authz surface beyond the already-scoped preferences form

tasks.title: Add email-address override input + unsubscribe-link route
tasks.description: Email override input defaults to the account email; unsubscribe link uses a signed token route that opens the preferences page with the relevant channel toggle pre-focused.
tasks.why: CAN-SPAM requires a working unsubscribe in every message; the override lets users route noise to a secondary inbox instead of opting out entirely.
tasks.what: Email override input defaulting to the account email, plus an unsubscribe route that validates a signed user+channel token and opens preferences with the channel toggle focused.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Email override saves and is used by the dispatcher in G3
Unsubscribe route validates the signed token before showing the form
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Sign tokens with Phoenix.Token using a dedicated salt and max_age
Token payload is {user_id, channel} only, verified server-side
Validate the override with the same email format check as registration
pitfalls: Unsubscribe must work without a login session (clicked from a mail client) but must not become an auth bypass into the rest of the app
Do not put the raw email address in the unsubscribe URL

unit_tests: Token round-trip: sign then verify yields {user_id, channel}; expired and tampered tokens are rejected
Email override changeset rejects invalid addresses
integration_tests: Controller test: valid token renders the form pre-focused; invalid or expired token renders an error without leaking account existence
manual_tests: Click an unsubscribe link from a rendered email in the dev mailbox
edge_cases: Token for a since-deleted user
Token reused after the user already unsubscribed — idempotent result

security_considerations: The signed, expiring token is the sole authz for unsubscribe — verify before any state change and scope it to unsubscribe only, never session auth
Validate email_override as a single address with no CR/LF — SMTP header-injection surface
Error responses must not disclose whether an account exists

goals.title: Render notification emails and dispatch via Oban worker
goals.why: Once events land on the queue (G1) and users have opted in (G2), the dispatcher reads the queue and emits actual emails.
goals.what: Build the email-rendering pipeline (shared shell + per-event-class templates), wire the Oban worker that drains the :notifications queue, and add the per-message unsubscribe footer.
goals.description: Depends on G1 (the queue contract). Claim G1 first; this goal becomes claimable once G1's queue + dedupe land in main.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Three event-class templates render (approval, mention, dependency-unblock)
Worker drains the queue and dispatches via the existing Mailer
Unsubscribe footer present in every email
Worker respects DND windows and channel opt-in from G2's preferences context
pitfalls: Do not bypass the existing audit-log infrastructure — every notification dispatch is logged
Do not send to a user whose preferences disable the channel

tasks.title: Define the email shell template (header, footer, unsubscribe link)
tasks.description: Shared HTML+text shell that wraps each event-class template. Includes the CAN-SPAM-compliant unsubscribe link with a signed token.
tasks.why: Every outgoing message shares one shell so the CAN-SPAM unsubscribe footer and branding cannot be forgotten by any per-class template.
tasks.what: Shared HTML and plain-text shell wrapping each event-class template, with header, footer, and a signed unsubscribe link on every message.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Shell renders for both HTML and plain-text variants
Unsubscribe link includes a signed user+channel token
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Render both HTML and text variants for every message
Build the unsubscribe token with the same Phoenix.Token salt/contract as G2's unsubscribe route
Build all links with verified route helpers
pitfalls: The plain-text variant rots easily — assert it in tests, not just the HTML
Do not inline token-signing here; call the shared helper so salts cannot drift from the unsubscribe route

unit_tests: Shell renders HTML and text variants with header, footer, and unsubscribe link present
Unsubscribe URL contains a verifiable signed token for the recipient and channel
integration_tests: Renderer composes shell plus a stub inner template end to end
manual_tests: Preview both variants in the dev mailbox for layout sanity
edge_cases: Inner template producing empty content still yields a valid shell
Very long inner content does not break the footer

security_considerations: The unsubscribe token must be signed and recipient-scoped — a guessable link lets anyone silence someone else's notifications
Everything interpolated into the HTML shell relies on EEx escaping; never use raw/1 on payload data

tasks.title: Render approval-owed email template
tasks.description: Per-event-class template for the approval flow. Plain text first; minimal HTML wrapper around it.
tasks.why: Approval-owed is the flagship event class; the email must carry enough context to act on without logging in blind.
tasks.what: Text-first approval-owed template plus a minimal HTML wrapper, rendered inside the shared shell with a deep link to the approval.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Template renders with the approval payload
Unit test asserts the rendered subject and body match the expected snapshot
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Plain text first; the HTML variant mirrors it
The subject-line pattern set here becomes the precedent for the other classes
Snapshot-test the rendered subject and body
pitfalls: Whole-body snapshot assertions break on copy tweaks — assert structure and key fields where copy is likely to change

unit_tests: Renders with a full approval payload; subject and body match the snapshot
Deep link targets the approval via route helpers
integration_tests: Renderer selects this template for :approval_owed events
manual_tests: Send to the dev mailbox and eyeball both variants
edge_cases: Very long task title truncates gracefully
Missing optional payload keys render without crashing
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Template render paths for both variants covered

security_considerations: Approval and task titles are user input — rely on EEx escaping in the HTML variant, no raw/1
Keep the body PII-light: names and titles, not full task descriptions

tasks.title: Render mention email template
tasks.description: Mention notification template; shows the comment excerpt + a deep link.
tasks.why: Mention emails embed user-written comment text — the one template where hostile input is guaranteed, so escaping discipline is set here.
tasks.what: Mention template showing the comment excerpt and a deep link to the comment, in text and HTML variants.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Template renders
Unit test covers escaping of user-supplied comment text
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Truncate the excerpt server-side to a fixed length before render
Deep link via route helpers, never a URL from the payload
Mirror approval_owed's subject conventions
pitfalls: Comment excerpts contain markup, emoji, and hostile strings — the escaping unit test in the acceptance criteria is the point of this task, not an afterthought

unit_tests: Renders with a normal excerpt
Excerpt containing script tags and HTML entities is escaped in the HTML variant
Excerpt truncation at the length cap
integration_tests: Renderer selects this template for :mention events
manual_tests: Dev-mailbox preview with an emoji-and-markup comment
edge_cases: Empty comment body
Multi-byte characters at the truncation boundary
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Escaping and truncation branches fully covered

security_considerations: Comment text is hostile input rendered into HTML mail — EEx auto-escaping must not be bypassed with raw/1 anywhere in this template
Deep link built from route helpers so a payload cannot smuggle an attacker-controlled URL into the email

tasks.title: Render dependency-unblocked email template
tasks.description: Per-event-class template for the dependency-unblock flow.
tasks.why: Completes the three-class template set so the dispatcher never encounters an event class it cannot render.
tasks.what: Dependency-unblocked template naming the unblocked task with a deep link; text variant per the acceptance criteria, HTML via the shared shell.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Template renders
Unit test asserts the rendered body names the unblocked task
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Mirror the structure and subject conventions of approval_owed and mention
Name both the unblocked task and the completed blocker in the body
pitfalls: G1's dedupe may deliver several unblocks in one merged payload — render a list, not just the first entry

unit_tests: Rendered body names the unblocked task
A merged payload with multiple unblocks renders all of them
integration_tests: Renderer selects this template for :dependency_unblocked events
edge_cases: Blocker task deleted between enqueue and render — the body degrades gracefully
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Single and merged-payload render paths covered

security_considerations: Task titles are user input — escaped at render; the body carries IDs and titles only, no task descriptions

tasks.title: Implement DispatchWorker that drains :notifications and respects preferences
tasks.description: Oban worker that pulls one job at a time, checks MyApp.Accounts.NotificationPreferences for channel_enabled? and dnd_active?, renders the appropriate template, and dispatches via the existing Mailer.
tasks.why: This worker is where the queue (G1) and preferences (G2) meet actual email — and where opt-in, DND, and audit compliance are enforced at send time.
tasks.what: Oban worker on :notifications that checks channel_enabled? and dnd_active?, renders the matching template, dispatches via the existing Mailer, and audit-logs each send.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Worker honors channel opt-in (skips if disabled)
Worker honors DND window (delays the job if active)
Audit-log entry written for every dispatch
Unit tests cover the opt-out, DND-active, and happy-path branches
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
use Oban.Worker with the :notifications queue and bounded max_attempts
Opt-out means discard with a reason; DND means snooze to the window end, never busy-retry
All preference checks go through the G2 context; resolve the recipient via email_override
pitfalls: A crash after Mailer.deliver but before the audit write double-sends on retry — order the audit write so retries are safe
DND is not an error; snoozed jobs must not consume attempts

unit_tests: Opt-out branch: job discarded, nothing sent, no sent-audit entry
DND branch: job snoozed until the window ends
Happy path: correct template rendered, Mailer invoked once, audit entry written
integration_tests: End to end: enqueue an event, run the worker via Oban.Testing, assert the delivered email via Swoosh test assertions
manual_tests: Trigger a real approval in dev and confirm the email arrives in the dev mailbox
edge_cases: Recipient deleted between enqueue and dispatch
Unknown event_class job discards with a logged reason instead of crash-looping
email_override set vs nil
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Every branch of the send/skip/snooze decision tree

security_considerations: Fail closed: any preference-lookup failure means skip, never send
Audit entries record recipient, event_class, and timestamp — not message bodies (PII minimization)
Resolve the address via the validated email_override, never from the job payload
Bounded retries prevent a retry storm from hammering the SMTP relay
